- Overestimate prices after recent spikes or positive sentiment, especially when sentiment is high or trending upward.  
- Underestimate prices during prolonged negative sentiment or when sentiment is trending downward.  
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment swings; model should not overshoot in direction unless sentiment is strongly sustained.  
- Mean-reversion bias is common in early forecast periods — model tends to overcorrect after sharp moves.  
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, reduce forecast magnitude and avoid extreme highs/lows.  
- For 30-day forecasts, lagged sentiment (especially 1-2 days prior) is a better predictor than current sentiment.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3-5 days, reduce forecast by 2-5% to account for downward pressure.  
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 3-5 days, increase forecast by 2-5% but cap at 10% to avoid overestimation.  
- Avoid forecasting sharp reversals unless sentiment is clearly turning — model should be conservative in horizon transitions.
